construct_scope: A modelled circadian component of sleep/wake regulation. It is not subjective fatigue, energy, mood, stress, melatonin concentration, core body temperature, SCN firing rate, or generic brain activity.

period_hours.meaning: Entrained circadian period used by the published Process C formulation.

phase.definition: phi determines the circadian phase position in clock hours. It is not assumed to equal CBTmin.
phase.schedule_source: The habitual wake entry in the configured prison regime schedule.

cbtmin_estimation.formula: estimated CBTmin interval = [habitual wake - 3 h, habitual wake - 2 h]
cbtmin_estimation.qualification: This interval is not a melatonin assay, core-body-temperature measurement, or direct circadian biomarker.

alignment.method: The implementation differentiates the published five-harmonic equation, numerically locates all stationary points over one 24-hour period, selects the global minimum, and subtracts that derived offset from the CBTmin interval to obtain a circular phi interval.

current_schedule_example.classification: OBSERVED CONFIGURATION plus SCHEDULE-BASED ESTIMATE plus DERIVED MATHEMATICALLY
current_schedule_example.note: This is an inspectable example for the current configuration, not a universal phase constant.

history.stored_evaluations: Actual runner evaluations are retained from installation onward; no older values are backfilled.
history.public_graph: The 1H, 24H and 7D curves are mathematically reconstructed from the latest stored schedule phase basis and are labelled as reconstructed rather than observed samples.

graph_coordinate_decimal_places.note: Inherited shared Soma graph rendering precision.

scn_phase_rotation_degrees_per_cycle.note: Direct circular unit conversion, not an activation coefficient.

provenance.citation: Borbely AA, Achermann P. Sleep homeostasis and models of sleep regulation. Journal of Biological Rhythms. 1999;14(6):557-568.
provenance.supports: Published five-harmonic Process C form, coefficients, and 24-hour period.

provenance.citation: Daan S, Beersma DGM, Borbely AA. Timing of human sleep: recovery process gated by a circadian pacemaker. American Journal of Physiology. 1984;246(2):R161-R178.
provenance.supports: Two-Process framework and circadian gating of sleep timing.

provenance.citation: Borbely AA. The two-process model of sleep regulation: Beginnings and outlook. Journal of Sleep Research. 2022;31(4):e13598.
provenance.supports: Modern review of the Two-Process model and its scope.

provenance.citation: Duffy JF et al. Sex difference in the near-24-hour intrinsic period of the human circadian timing system. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences. 2011;108(Suppl 3):15602-15608.
provenance.supports: Measured CBT nadir occurred on average about three hours before habitual wake, with substantial individual variation; used only to justify a broad schedule-based estimate, not direct phase observation.

explicit_limitations.subjective_fatigue_mapping: PROVISIONAL - Process S and Process C are exposed separately; no weights, intercept, threshold, or combined fatigue equation is implemented.
explicit_limitations.grounded_prompt_projection: The schedule-estimated Process C value and uncertainty may be supplied factually to the language model; no subjective Fatigue or other state is inferred.
